name: 31660-loradecode-qwen3moe30b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3, one GPU of an a3 node, driver 570.195.03
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1 -- one engine, one card, no sharding; `fully_sharded_loras` left at its default (off)
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=32, bounded at 320 requests with a 1800 s safety cap, warmup the first 10% and cooldown the last 10% by completion.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix buckets, no tools: fixed-shape random-token requests, 2048 prompt tokens and exactly 1024 output tokens, both pinned min=max and the output length made exact by `max_tokens=1024` with `ignore_eos=True`. `request_format: plain`, so the wire prompt is the declared 2048 tokens with no chat template. Greedy (temperature 0.0), prefix caching off, and every request carries the LoRA adapter.
purpose: A LoRA-adapted 30-billion-parameter assistant drafting 1024-token answers from 2048-token briefs, 32 concurrent users, single GPU.
launch:
# Launch config for 31660-loradecode-qwen3moe30b-1gpu. Every key goes straight into
# AsyncEngineArgs; nothing here was searched for.

model: Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B
tensor-parallel-size: 1

enable-lora: true
max-loras: 1
# Follows the adapter actually loaded (adapter_config.json: r=8). It sizes the stacked LoRA
# buffers, so a larger value pads every one of them with zeros and measures padding.
max-lora-rank: 8

enable-prefix-caching: false
max-num-seqs: 128
# Pinned, not chosen. The in-process path builds the engine with UsageContext.ENGINE_CONTEXT,
# which is in no per-context default table, so an unpinned run falls through to 2048.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
max-model-len: 4096
# Above the engine's 0.90 default: ~57 GiB of bf16 weights is large relative to an 80 GB card.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.93
dtype: bfloat16
